title: Stone Soup
author: Traditional; adapted for Shellfie
credit: An original adaptation of the traditional folktale Stone Soup, written for Shellfie. The stone is part of the make-believe story; do not put stones in food.

pages: A traveler came to a village at lunchtime. “I am hungry,” the traveler said, “but I have no food to share.”
A neighbor brought out a big pot of water. “We can make pretend stone soup,” the traveler said with a smile.
The traveler held up a smooth stone. “Let us imagine it is in the pot. Real soup needs real food!”
“I have a carrot,” said one neighbor. The carrot went into the pot, and the water began to bubble.
“I have a potato,” said another. Soon a third neighbor brought peas, and someone else brought an onion.
Everyone stirred and waited. The kitchen filled with a warm, tasty smell, and the neighbors gathered around.
When the soup was ready, the traveler gave everyone a bowl. There was enough for the whole table.
“Our soup tastes good because we shared,” a neighbor said. The traveler smiled, and everyone ate together.

quiz.q: What did the first neighbor add to the pot?
quiz.ev: “I have a carrot,” said one neighbor.

quiz.q: Why was there enough soup for everyone?
quiz.ev: “Our soup tastes good because we shared,” a neighbor said.
The kitchen filled with a warm, tasty smell, and the neighbors gathered around.
